text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A new finance ministry report on the public sector shows that users of public institutions are content with, among others, dentists, the National Museum and libraries while fewer Danes are content with job centres, study grants, legal courts and emergency medical service.

--- The competition board demanded on Wednesday that Denmark's two largest dairies MD Foods and Kloever Maelk change their near-monopolistic alliance. At present the two firms process 90 percent of the milk in Denmark and the board believes that they have used this position to fix milk prices for large retailers, thereby hindering competition.
--- A Dane Jakob Simonsen, head of the United Nations development department in Lima, Peru, is among the 400-500 hostages held by left-wing guerrillas at the Japanese ambassador's house in Lima.

--- Research minister Frank Jensen says he wants to strengthen research cooperation between foreign companies and Danish universities and other institutions of higher education, contrary to reports that he is reluctant to let foreign companies benefit from Danish tax-financed research.
